(Section)

Among those is His, glorified and exalted, oath: ﴿By the night when it covers, and the day when it displays itself, and by Him who created the male and the female﴾.

The oath regarding this has already been mentioned, and that [the verse concerns] the striving of man in this world and his recompense in the Hereafter. So He, glorified, swears by the night in all its states, since it is among His signs that point to Him, and He swore by it at the time of its covering. He used the present tense (yaghshā) because it covers one thing after another. As for the day, when the sun rises it appears and displays itself all at once. For this reason He said in Surat ash-Shams: ﴿And by the day when it displays it, and by the night when it covers it﴾, and He swore by it at the time of its spreading out, as has been mentioned. He also swore by it at the time of its retreating, and He swore by it when it "ʿasʿasa" (began to withdraw or to come). It was said that its meaning is "adbara" (it turned back), which corresponds to His saying ﴿And by the night when it retreats, and by the morning when it brightens﴾. It was also said that its meaning is "aqbala" (it came forward), which would be like His saying ﴿By the night when it covers, and the day when it displays itself﴾.

Thus He has sworn by the approach of both the night and the day.

According to the first view, the oath falls upon the passing of the night and the coming of the day after it, and both are among the signs of His lordship.

Then He swore by the creation of the male and the female. This includes swearing by all animals with their varied kinds, male and female, and He contrasted the male and the female just as He contrasted the night and the day, and all of this is among the signs of His lordship. For the bringing forth of night and day through the heavenly bodies is like the bringing forth of male and female through the lower bodies. He brings forth from the earth the males and females of animals, of their varied kinds, just as He brings forth from the sky the night and the day by means of the sun in it. And He, glorified, swore by the time of striving, which is the night and the day, and by the striver, who is male and female, with their differing striving, just as the night and day differ, and the male and female differ, and their striving and their time differ. This is a proof that their recompense and reward differ, and that He, glorified, does not equate between those whose striving differs in the recompense, just as He did not equate between the night and the day, or the male and the female.

Then He informed of His distinction between the outcome of the striving of the good-doer and the outcome of the striving of the evil-doer, saying: ﴿As for him who gives and fears [God], and affirms the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease. But as for him who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best [reward], We will ease him toward hardship﴾.

The two verses include the mention of His law, the mention of deeds and their recompense, and the wisdom of divine decree in facilitating this one toward ease and that one toward hardship, and that the servant is made easy by his deeds toward their ends, and your Lord does not wrong anyone. The mention of facilitation toward ease contains three causes. The first is "giving" by the servant, and the object of the verb is omitted, intending generality and comprehensiveness: i.e., he gives what he was commanded to give, and what his nature allowed and his soul obeyed. This includes his giving from himself faith, obedience, sincerity, repentance and gratitude, and his giving of goodness and benefit with his wealth, tongue, body, intention and aim. So his soul becomes an obedient, generous soul, not a stingy, withholding one. The obedient soul is the beneficial, good-doing soul whose nature is goodness and the giving of both obligatory and extended good, so it gives its good to itself and to others. It is like the spring from which people benefit by drinking, watering their animals, livestock and crops, and they benefit from it however they wish. It is thus made easy for that. Likewise the blessed man is made easy for benefit wherever he settles, so the recompense for this is that Allah makes him easy toward ease, just as his soul was made easy for giving.

The second cause is taqwā (fear of God), which is avoiding what Allah has forbidden. This is among the greatest causes of facilitation, and its opposite is among the causes of difficulty. The God-fearing person has his affairs of this world and the Hereafter made easy for him, whereas the one who abandons taqwā, even if some of his worldly affairs are made easy for him, becomes burdened in matters of his Hereafter according to what he has abandoned of taqwā. As for the facilitation of what is made easy for him of worldly affairs: if he had feared Allah, its facilitation would have been more complete. And even if it be supposed that it was not made easy for him, Allah has made easy for him from the world what is more beneficial for him than what he attained without taqwā, for good living, the bliss of the heart, the delight and joy and exhilaration of the soul are among the greatest blessings of this world, and they are greater than the blessings of the people of the world who seek desires and pleasures.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair﴾.

So He informed that He makes easy for the God-fearing what He does not make easy for others. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out, and provide for him from where he does not expect﴾.

This too is made easy for him by his taqwā. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will remove from him his misdeeds and magnify for him a reward﴾.

This is made easy for him by the removal of what he fears and the granting of what he loves and is pleased with. He said: ﴿O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqān) and will expiate from you your misdeeds and forgive you﴾.

This is made easy by the furqān, which includes deliverance, victory, knowledge, and the light that distinguishes truth from falsehood, along with the expiation of misdeeds and forgiveness of sins, and that is the ultimate ease. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And fear Allah that you may prosper﴾. And success is the ultimate ease, just as misery is the ultimate hardship. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy, and will make for you a light by which you walk, and will forgive you﴾. So He, glorified, guaranteed them through taqwā three things. First: He gave them two portions of His mercy, a portion in this world and a portion in the Hereafter, and the portion of the Hereafter may be multiplied for them, so it becomes two portions. Second: He gave them a light by which they walk in darknesses. Third: forgiveness of their sins. This is the ultimate ease. So He, glorified, made taqwā a cause of every ease, and abandonment of taqwā a cause of every hardship.

The third cause is affirming the best (al-ḥusnā). It has been interpreted as "lā ilāha illā Allāh" (there is no god but Allah), it has been interpreted as Paradise, and it has been interpreted as the replacement (khalaf), and these are the sayings of the early scholars (salaf). "Al-yusrā" is an attribute of a omitted noun, meaning "the state and the condition of ease," and it is the feminine form of "al-yusr." The three sayings return to the best deeds and the best recompense. Whoever interprets it as "lā ilāha illā Allāh" has interpreted it as a single term that comprises every category, for true affirmation of "lā ilāha illā Allāh" entails affirmation of all its branches and sub-branches, and all the roots and branches of religion are among the branches of this word. The servant does not affirm it in its true sense until he believes in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the meeting with Him. Nor is he a believer in Allah, the God of the worlds, until he believes in the attributes of His majesty and the descriptions of His perfection. Nor is he a believer that Allah is the only God until he denies the characteristics of divinity from every existent other than Him, and denies them from his own belief and will, as they are in truth and in reality negated. Nor is he one who affirms it if he negates the lofty attributes, or negates His speech and His addressing, or negates His istiwā' over His throne, and that the good word and righteous deed ascend to Him, and that He raised Christ to Himself, and that He carried His messenger up to Him, and that He governs the affair from heaven to earth, then it ascends to Him, and all the other things He described Himself with and His messenger described Him with. Nor is he a true believer and affirmer of this word who denies the comprehensiveness of His creation over everything, His power over everything, His knowledge of everything, and the resurrection of bodies from graves for the Day of Rising.

Nor is he one who affirms it if he claims that He leaves His creation neglected, not commanding them or forbidding them through His messengers. Likewise, affirming it requires submission and acknowledgment of its rights, which are the laws of Islam, the detailed explanation of this word: by affirming all His reports, executing His commands, and avoiding His prohibitions, which is the detailed explanation of "lā ilāha illā Allāh." So the one who truly affirms it is the one who does all of that. Likewise, the protection of wealth and blood in the absolute sense is attained only by it and by upholding its rights. Likewise, deliverance from punishment in the absolute sense is attained only by it and by its rights. So the punishment in this world and the Hereafter is for abandoning it or abandoning its rights.

Whoever interprets "al-ḥusnā" as Paradise has interpreted it as the highest kind of recompense and its perfection. Whoever interprets it as the replacement has mentioned a kind of recompense; this is worldly recompense, while Paradise is the recompense in the Hereafter. So affirmation of the best returns to affirmation of faith and its recompense. The verification is that it encompasses both matters.

Consider what these three words contain: giving, taqwā, and affirming the best, of knowledge and action, and what they include of guidance and the religion of truth. The soul has three faculties: the faculty of giving and spending, the faculty of restraint and abstention, and the faculty of perception and understanding. In it is the faculty of knowledge and awareness, followed by the faculty of love and will, and the faculty of hatred and aversion. These three faculties are the axis of its righteousness and happiness, and by their corruption comes its corruption and wretchedness. Corruption of the faculty of knowledge and awareness necessitates denial of the best; corruption of the faculty of love and will necessitates abandoning giving; corruption of the faculty of hatred and aversion necessitates abandoning taqwā. So when the faculty of love and will is perfected by giving what he was commanded, and the faculty of hatred and aversion by avoiding what he was forbidden, and the faculty of knowledge and awareness by affirming the word of Islam, its rights and its recompense, he has purified his soul and prepared it for every state of ease, and the soul thereby becomes made easy for ease.

Since religion turns on three foundations: doing what is commanded, abandoning what is forbidden, and affirming the report; or if you wish, religion is demand and report, and demand is of two kinds, demand of action and demand of abstention, these three words contain the most comprehensive levels of religion. Giving is doing what is commanded, taqwā is abandoning what is forbidden, and affirming the best is affirming the report. Thus all of religion is included. The most perfect people are those in whom these three taqwās are complete, and deficiency enters in proportion to their lack or partial lack. Among people there is one whose capacity for giving is more complete than his capacity for restraint, so his capacity for abstention is weaker than his capacity for giving. Among people there is one whose capacity for restraint and abstention is more complete than his capacity for giving and withholding. Among people there is one in whom the capacity for affirmation is more complete than the capacity for giving and withholding, so his cognitive and perceptive capacity is more complete than his volitional capacity, and vice versa. Deficiency enters in proportion to the lack in these three faculties, and he misses of the facilitation toward ease in proportion to what he has missed of them. Whoever has these faculties complete is made easy for every ease.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: ﴿We will ease him toward ease﴾, i.e., We will prepare him for the work of good; the works of good are made easy for him. Muqātil, al-Kalbī and al-Farrāʾ said: We will ease him to return to righteous action.

The reality of "al-yusrā" is the state and condition that is easy and beneficial, which befalls him, and it is the opposite of "al-ʿusrā."

That includes His making easy for him goodness and its causes, so goodness flows and is made easy upon his heart, hands, tongue and limbs, and the qualities of goodness become easy for him, subdued to him and submissive, not resisting him.

They are not difficult, because he is prepared for them and made easy to perform them; he treads their paths easily, and they are led to him in knowledge and action. When you accompany him, you say: he is the one about whom it was said:

*Blessed of countenance, auspicious of presence,*
*fit for this world and for religion.*

﴿And as for him who withholds and considers himself self-sufficient﴾, who has idled the faculty of will and giving from doing what he was commanded, ﴿considers himself self-sufficient﴾ by abandoning taqwā before his Lord, idling the faculty of restraint and abstention from doing what he was forbidden, ﴿and denies the best﴾, idling the faculty of knowledge and awareness from affirming faith and its recompense, ﴿We will ease him toward hardship.﴾

ʿAṭāʾ said: I will come between his heart and faith in Me and My messenger.

Muqātil said: It becomes difficult for him to give any good.

ʿIkrima reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: We will ease him for evil.

al-Wāḥidī said: This is the view, for evil leads to punishment, so it is the hardship state, and good leads to ease and comfort in Paradise, so it is the easy state. The meaning is: We will prepare him for evil by letting it flow through his hands.

al-Farrāʾ said: The Arabs say: "The sheep of so-and-so became easy," when they were ready for giving birth, and likewise when they gave birth and their milk became abundant, meaning that they made that easy for their owners. End of quote.

Facilitation toward hardship occurs in two ways:

First, that He comes between him and the causes of good, so evil flows upon his heart, intention, tongue and limbs.

Second, that He comes between him and the easier recompense, just as He came between him and its causes.

If it is said: How did he pair "taqwā" with "istaghnā" (self-sufficiency), and is it possible for a servant to be self-sufficient of his Lord even for the blink of an eye?

It is answered: This is one of the finest pairings, for the God-fearing person, when he senses his poverty, neediness and his great need for his Lord, fears Him and does not expose himself to His anger, wrath and hatred by committing what He forbade. For one who is in great need and dependence upon a person fears his anger and displeasure to the utmost, avoids what he dislikes to the utmost, and relies on doing what He loves and prefers. So He paired taqwā with self-sufficiency to disgrace the state of the one who abandons taqwā, and to emphasize his blame, by making him act as one self-sufficient of his Lord, not as a poor one who is compelled toward Him, who has no refuge but Him and no independence from His grace, generosity and kindness for the blink of an eye. How sweet is this pairing, and how comprehensive are these two verses of all goods and their causes, and all evils and their causes. Glorified is He who made Himself known to the particular qualities of His servants through His speech, and manifested Himself to them therein; they do not seek a trace after an essence, nor exchange truth for falsehood, nor sincerity for deceit.

These two verses contain the decisive word in the question of qadar (divine decree), and the removal of every confusion and difficulty concerning it, which by God's praise is clear to whoever is granted understanding of it. For this reason the Prophet answered with them the one who raised the question that people never cease to repeat about qadar. He answered with the decisive word and removed the difficulty. In the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, that he said:

"There is none of you but his place has been known, in Paradise or in the Fire."

It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we not leave off action and rely upon the Book?" He said: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for."

Then he recited: ﴿As for him who gives and fears [God], and affirms the best [reward], We will ease him toward ease﴾.

This hadith contains a refutation of the Qadariyya and the Jabriyya, an affirmation of qadar and of the law, and an affirmation of the first Book which contains Allah's knowledge of things before their existence, and an affirmation of the creation of the act as recompense. It refutes the foundations of the Qadariyya who deny the creation of acts absolutely; and whoever among them acknowledges the creation of the act of recompense but not of the beginning has demolished his own principle and undermined his foundation. The Prophet ﷺ reported the same as what the Lord, exalted, reported: that the servant is made easy for what he was created for, not compelled. So "compulsion" (jabr) is a innovated term, while "facilitation" (taysīr) is the term of the Qur'an and the Sunnah.

In the hadith there is an indication that the Companions were the most knowledgeable of people in the foundations of religion, for they received them from the one most knowledgeable of creation about Allah in the absolute sense, and whenever they found something problematic they asked him about it, and he answered them with what removes the difficulty and makes the right clear. They are thus the true knowers of the foundations of religion, not the people of innovation and desires among the theologians, nor those who follow their way. In the hadith there is also the Prophet ﷺ's use of the Qur'an as evidence on the matters of the foundations of religion, and his guidance of the Companions to derive them from it, contrary to those who claim that the speech of Allah and His Messenger does not yield certainty regarding any of the foundations of religion, and that knowledge of Allah, His names, attributes and acts cannot be derived from them, and who express this by saying: "Verbal evidences do not produce certainty."

In the hadith there is a clarification that among people some are created for happiness and some are created for wretchedness, contrary to those who claim that they are all created for happiness but chose wretchedness and were not created for it. It also contains the affirmation of causes, and that the servant is made easy for the causes that lead him to what he was created for. It also contains evidence that the Sunnah is derived from the Book and conforms to it. Reflect on his ﷺ saying "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for," and its correspondence to Allah's saying ﴿As for him who gives and fears﴾ through the end of the two verses, how the law, the decree, the cause and the effect are all brought together.

This is the guidance that the Prophet pointed to, and it is the nature with which God created His servants. Even irrational animals and the worldly interests and prosperity of this life are built on it. If every person said, "If it is decreed for me to have such-and-such, I will certainly attain it, and if it is not decreed, there is no way to obtain it, so I will neither strive nor move," he would be counted among the foolish and ignorant, and he could never keep this up. Even if he applied it to one specific matter, could he apply it to all his worldly interests: his food, drink, clothing, shelter, and fleeing from what threatens his survival and harms his welfare? Or does he find himself unable to separate from the Prophet's saying, "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for"? If this applies to the interests of this world and the causes of its benefits, what justifies neglecting it in the interests of the Hereafter and the causes of happiness and success there? The Lord of this world and the Hereafter is one. How, then, could this be suspended in the law and command of the Lord and applied only to the servant's will, desires, and appetites? Is this anything but pure injustice and ignorance? "Man is indeed a wrongdoer and ignorant": a wrongdoer to himself and ignorant of his Lord. This is what the Prophet pointed to when he recited these two verses in his presence. It agrees with what God placed in the minds of rational people and built into the natural disposition of all creatures, even irrational animals. He sent all His messengers with it and revealed all His books with it.

If the servant relied on divine decree (qadar) and did not act, the sacred laws (shari'ah) would be suspended, the interests of the world would be disrupted, and both worldly and religious affairs would be corrupted. Only those who abandon the sacred laws take comfort in this, and those who cast off the commands and prohibitions from their necks. This is an inheritance from their idolatrous brethren who rejected God's command and prohibition and opposed His law with His decree and predestination, as God relates of them in more than one place in His Book. Such as His words: ﴿The idolaters will say: "If God had willed, we would not have associated anything with Him, nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything." Likewise did those before them deny until they tasted Our might. Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can bring out for us? You follow only conjecture, and you merely guess." Say: "To God belongs the conclusive proof. Had He willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ And His words: ﴿Those who associated partners said: "If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything apart from Him." Likewise did those before them act. Is there upon the messengers anything but clear delivery?﴾ And His words: ﴿They say: "If the Most Merciful had willed, we would not have worshipped them." They have no knowledge of that; they only guess.﴾

And His words: ﴿When it is said to them: "Spend from what God has provided you," those who disbelieve say to those who believe: "Shall we feed one whom God, if He willed, would feed? You are only in clear error."﴾

If it is said: giving, piety, and affirming the best reward belong to ease, indeed they are the root of ease. Who made them easy for the servant in the first place? The same applies to their opposites. It is said: God is the One who made the causes of good and evil easy for the servant. He created His creatures in two categories: people of happiness, whom He made easy for ease, and people of wretchedness, whom He made easy for hardship. He employs each group in the causes for which they were created, and they are fit for nothing else. His overwhelming wisdom refuses to place His punishment where it does not belong, just as it refuses to place His honor and reward where they are not fitting or suitable. Indeed, even the wisdom of individual creatures refuses this. Whoever treats musk and dung as the same is among the most foolish of fools.

If it is asked: why is this one fit only for honor, and that one fit only for humiliation? It is answered: this is the question of an ignorant person who does not deserve an answer. It is as if he were saying: why did God create this and that?

If it is asked: given this, does this ignorant person have an answer that might cure him of his ignorance?

It is answered: yes. The nature of lordship is to create things and their opposites, and to create necessary things and what they necessitate. Thus, height necessitates lowness and is necessitated by it; night necessitates day and is necessitated by it. The perfection of this existence lies in heat and cold, clear skies and clouds. Among the necessities of animal nature are health and sickness, and the variation of wills and what is willed. The existence of a necessity without what it necessitates is impossible. Had the opposites not been created, the perfection of power, will, and wisdom would not be known, and the effects of the divine names and attributes would not appear.

The manifestation of their effects and consequences is necessary, for it is required by perfect sacredness and complete sovereignty. If you give the name "King" its due, and you cannot, you will know that creation, command, reward and punishment, bestowal and withholding are necessary consequences of the attribute of sovereignty, and that the attribute of sovereignty necessarily requires them. The suspension of this attribute is impossible. True sovereignty requires the sending of messengers, the revelation of books, the commanding and forbidding of servants, their reward and punishment, honoring those who deserve honor, and humiliating those who deserve humiliation. Just as the life, knowledge, will, power, hearing, sight, speech, mercy, pleasure, and anger of a king, and his sitting upon his throne directing the affairs of his servants, are necessitated by his kingship. This indication suffices the intelligent person in such a matter, and through it he will be shown a fertile land and treasures of knowledge. And success is from God.

(Another section)

As for the oaths concerning the states of man, such as His words: ﴿By the night when it covers, by the day when it appears, by Him who created the male and the female: indeed, your efforts are diverse.﴾

The word sa'y ("striving, effort") means action, but it refers to action to which its doer applies great concern and strives as much as possible. If it requires running with the body, one runs; if it requires gathering one's helpers, one gathers them; if it requires devoting oneself to it and abandoning other things, one does so. The word sa'y in the Qur'an is used in this sense. It is not synonymous with the word 'amal ("action"), as some have thought. Rather, it is a specific action to which its doer applies concern and effort. For this reason, He said regarding Friday: ﴿hasten to the remembrance of God﴾.

This is better than the reading of those who recite "proceed to the remembrance of God" (fam-du).

It is established in the Sahih, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When the prayer is established, do not come to it running. Come walking, with tranquility upon you. Whatever you catch, pray; and whatever you miss, complete."

He did not forbid striving toward prayer, for God commanded striving toward it. Rather, he forbade them from coming to it running. So he forbade coming in a manner characterized by the haste of its doer. Coming is an action of the body, and striving with it is running with the body, which is forbidden.

As for the striving commanded in the verse, it is going to prayer with concern for it, devoting oneself to it, abandoning distracting activities such as trade and others, and turning the heart toward striving for it.

Likewise His words in the story of Pharaoh, when Moses said to him: ﴿Is there for you a way to purify yourself, and I will guide you to your Lord so that you may fear Him?﴾ Then he showed him the greatest sign, but he denied and disobeyed. Then he turned away, striving; so he gathered and called out. This is concern and effort in gathering his subjects and calling to them.

Likewise His words: ﴿And when he turns away, he strives in the earth to cause corruption therein.﴾ This is action with determination and effort. From this comes the name of the one who collects alms (sa'i), and the one who cares for the widow and the orphan.

From it also comes His words: ﴿indeed, your efforts are diverse.﴾ It is the action that its doer intends and attends to, so that reward or punishment follows from it, unlike ordinary permissible acts, which are not included in this striving. God says: ﴿As for he who gives and fears God and affirms the best reward, We will ease him toward ease. And as for he who is miserly and considers himself self-sufficient and denies the best reward, We will ease him toward hardship.﴾ From it also comes His words: ﴿And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it as it should be striven for, while being a believer﴾, and His words: ﴿The penalty of those who wage war against God and His Messenger and strive upon the earth for corruption is only that﴾.

(A benefit)

It is authentically reported from him (ﷺ) that he was asked about the matter of predestination and what people do in it: is it a matter already decreed and finished, or a matter yet to be determined? He said: "Rather, it is a matter already decreed and finished." He was then asked: "Then why do we act?" He answered: "Act, for each is made easy for what he was created for. As for one among the people of happiness, he will be made easy for the works of the people of happiness, and as for one among the people of wretchedness, he will be made easy for the works of the people of wretchedness." Then he recited His words: ﴿As for he who gives and fears God and affirms the best reward...﴾ until the end of the two verses.

Narrated by Muslim.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 92, verses 12–13:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance, and indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life.﴾

It was said that its meaning is: indeed, it is upon Us to make clear the path of guidance from the path of misguidance.

Qatadah said: "Upon Allah is the clarification, the clarification of what is lawful and unlawful, obedience and disobedience."

Abu Ishaq (al-Zajjaj) chose this view, and it is the view of Muqatil and a group [of scholars]. This meaning is true, but the intended meaning of the verse is something else.

It was also said that the meaning is: indeed, upon Us is guidance and misguidance.

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said in the narration of Ata: "He means: I guide My friends to acting in My obedience, and I prevent My enemies from being able to act in My obedience." Al-Farra said: "He omitted mention of misguidance, as in His saying ﴿and garments that protect you from the heat﴾, meaning and the cold."

This view is weaker than the first view. Although its meaning is correct, it is not the meaning of the verse.

It was also said that the meaning is: whoever takes the path of guidance, upon Allah is [the making of] his way straight, like His saying ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾.

This is the view of Mujahid, and it is the most sound of the views on the verse. Al-Wahidi said: "Upon Us is guidance" means that guidance brings its possessor to Allah, to His reward and His Paradise.

This meaning appears in the Qur'an in three places: here, in Surah al-Nahl in His saying ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾, and in Surah al-Hijr in His saying ﴿This is a straight path upon Me﴾. It is a noble and magnificent meaning, indicating that the one who travels the path of guidance is certainly led by that path to Allah. Guidance is the straight path, so whoever follows it, it brings him to Allah. Thus the path is mentioned together with the goal: the path is guidance, and the goal is arrival at Allah. These are the highest of means and their goal is the highest of goals.

Since the seeker's aim toward Allah is to attain the benefits of his worldly life and his Hereafter, this aim is not fulfilled for him except by unifying his seeking and the One from whom he seeks. So He, glory be to Him, informed him that other than Him possesses nothing of this world or the Hereafter, and that the world and the Hereafter are wholly His alone. When the servant is certain of this, his seeking and his object of seeking converge upon the One who alone owns this world and the Hereafter.

Thus the two verses comprise four matters, which are the lofty aims: the mention of the highest goal, which is arrival at Allah, glory be to Him; the nearest of ways and means to Him, which is the way of guidance; the unification of the path, so that one does not deviate from it to another; and the unification of the object sought, which is the Truth, so that one does not turn from it to another. Draw these matters from the niche of these words, for this is the summit of knowledge and understanding. And success is from Allah.

Complete guidance includes the unification of the object sought, the unification of the seeking, and the unification of the path that leads there. Cutting off and failure to arrive occur through association (shirk) in these matters, or some of them. Association in the object sought contradicts tawhid and sincerity; association in the seeking contradicts truthfulness and resolve; association in the path contradicts following the command. The first leads to shirk and ostentation (riya'), the second leads to disobedience and idleness, and the third leads to innovation (bid'ah) and departure from the Sunnah. So reflect upon this.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 92, verses 12–13:

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance, and indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life.﴾

It was said that its meaning is: indeed, it is upon Us to make clear the path of guidance from the path of misguidance.

Qatadah said: "Upon Allah is the clarification, the clarification of what is lawful and unlawful, obedience and disobedience."

Abu Ishaq (al-Zajjaj) chose this view, and it is the view of Muqatil and a group [of scholars]. This meaning is true, but the intended meaning of the verse is something else.

It was also said that the meaning is: indeed, upon Us is guidance and misguidance.

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said in the narration of Ata: "He means: I guide My friends to acting in My obedience, and I prevent My enemies from being able to act in My obedience." Al-Farra said: "He omitted mention of misguidance, as in His saying ﴿and garments that protect you from the heat﴾, meaning and the cold."

This view is weaker than the first view. Although its meaning is correct, it is not the meaning of the verse.

It was also said that the meaning is: whoever takes the path of guidance, upon Allah is [the making of] his way straight, like His saying ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾.

This is the view of Mujahid, and it is the most sound of the views on the verse. Al-Wahidi said: "Upon Us is guidance" means that guidance brings its possessor to Allah, to His reward and His Paradise.

This meaning appears in the Qur'an in three places: here, in Surah al-Nahl in His saying ﴿And upon Allah is the direction of the way﴾, and in Surah al-Hijr in His saying ﴿This is a straight path upon Me﴾. It is a noble and magnificent meaning, indicating that the one who travels the path of guidance is certainly led by that path to Allah. Guidance is the straight path, so whoever follows it, it brings him to Allah. Thus the path is mentioned together with the goal: the path is guidance, and the goal is arrival at Allah. These are the highest of means and their goal is the highest of goals.

Since the seeker's aim toward Allah is to attain the benefits of his worldly life and his Hereafter, this aim is not fulfilled for him except by unifying his seeking and the One from whom he seeks. So He, glory be to Him, informed him that other than Him possesses nothing of this world or the Hereafter, and that the world and the Hereafter are wholly His alone. When the servant is certain of this, his seeking and his object of seeking converge upon the One who alone owns this world and the Hereafter.

Thus the two verses comprise four matters, which are the lofty aims: the mention of the highest goal, which is arrival at Allah, glory be to Him; the nearest of ways and means to Him, which is the way of guidance; the unification of the path, so that one does not deviate from it to another; and the unification of the object sought, which is the Truth, so that one does not turn from it to another. Draw these matters from the niche of these words, for this is the summit of knowledge and understanding. And success is from Allah.

The first leads to shirk and ostentation (riya'), the second leads to disobedience and idleness, and the third leads to innovation (bid'ah) and departure from the Sunnah. So reflect upon this.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 92, verses 14–16:

When He, glorified is He, had established the proof, lit up the path, clarified the argument and explained the clear way, He warned His servants of His punishment, which He has prepared for those who deny His report and turn away from His obedience. He made this category of people the most wretched of them, just as He made the most fortunate of them the people of taqwa (God-consciousness), ihsan (excellence) and ikhlas (sincerity). This category is the one that is kept away from His punishment, as He said: ﴿And the most God-conscious will be kept away from it, who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾. This muttaqi, muhsin one does not do that except seeking the Face of his Lord, so he is sincere in his taqwa and his ihsan.

In the verse there is guidance that the person of taqwa should not accept favours from creation and their kindnesses; and if he does accept something from them, he hastens to repay them for it, so that no one among creation has a favour upon him that needs to be repaid, and thus his whole deed is for Allah alone, and there is no recompense owed to the created being for his favour.

By His words ﴿tujza (is repaid)﴾ He draws attention to the fact that the favour of Islam which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had upon this most God-conscious one cannot be repaid. Every possessor of a favour can have his favour repaid, except the favour of Islam, for the one who bestowed it cannot be repaid with it. This shows that al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), may Allah be pleased with him, is the first and most deserving of those mentioned in this verse, and that he is the most entitled of the Ummah to it. For ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, was raised in the house of the Prophet (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah had with him a favour other than the favour of Islam that could be repaid.

By His words ﴿except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High﴾ He, glorified is He, points out that the one upon whom no created being has a favour that needs repaying does not do what he does except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High, unlike one who is bound by the favours and kindnesses of created beings, for he is compelled to act for their sake and to refrain for their sake. For this reason, it is among the perfection of sincerity that the servant does not place upon himself an obligation to anyone among people, so that all his dealings are for Allah, seeking His Face and seeking His pleasure. Just as this aim is the highest of aims and this objective the most noble of objectives, so this path is the most direct and nearest and most upright route to it. And success is from Allah.

(Benefit)

Ibn al-Qayyim said, after some discussion:

Like the delusion of some people regarding His words about the Fire: ﴿None will burn therein except the most wretched, who denied and turned away﴾ [al-Layl: 15–16], and His words: ﴿prepared for the disbelievers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 24].

This deluded person does not realise that His words ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes﴾ refer to a specific Fire from among the levels of Jahannam; and even if it were all of Jahannam, He, glorified is He, did not say "none will enter it", but said ﴿none will burn therein except the most wretched﴾. The absence of burning does not necessarily entail the absence of entering, for *al-salyu* (burning) is more specific than *al-dukhul* (entering), and negating the more specific does not entail negating the more general.

Then, if this deluded person had reflected on the verse that follows it, he would have known that he is not included in it, and so it is not guaranteed for him that he will be kept away from it.

(Subtle point)

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And no one has upon him a favour to be repaid, except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High﴾

He made the ultimate aim of the deeds of the righteous, the near ones, and the lovers: the desire for His Face.
